usage: This is the standard, everyday greeting in Cairo used to ask how someone is doing. It is appropriate for almost all situations, from casual chats with friends to everyday interactions with shopkeepers or colleagues. For highly formal situations, such as speaking to a boss or an elder, Egyptians add the word for respect, 7adretak.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: The standard casual greeting addressed to a single male.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: The standard casual greeting addressed to a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: formal to a man
variants.note: Used to show respect to an older man, a boss, or a stranger.

variants.label: casual alternative
variants.note: A very common, slightly more conversational alternative meaning what are you doing.

examples.arabic: إِزَّيَّك يا أَحْمَد؟ عاش مِين شافَك.
examples.english: How are you, Ahmed? Long time no see.

examples.transliteration: ezzayyoko ya shabab? eh el akhbar?
examples.english: How are you guys? What is the news?
